scope: Synthetic POSIX/Linux file operations by dropped-privilege child processes. No native coding agent, model, native logging, native session resume or built-in edit route was run. Legitimate-operation controls are synthetic proxies.
environment_note: Cloud sandbox VM (not the project's baseline Docker image sha256:eddc3b19...; no Docker daemon available). The baseline-image run is the teammate's, in research/reviews/permission-probe-02-docker/.
not_run_classification: From the recorded not_run_reason: a reason starting 'not applicable:' is not applicable to the layout; 'the recorder identity could not open the descriptor' is a precondition the layout itself refused; every other reason (or none) means the cell could not be executed in this environment.

protection_assessment.rule: Three-valued. A layout HOLDS a requirement only if every required cell was executed and gave the good verdict. It FAILS if at least one required cell was executed and gave the bad verdict (a tampering effect, a denied proxy, an observed suppression); that is a determined result even if other cells are missing. Otherwise, if any required cell was not executed in this environment or ended in unexpected_error, the layout is UNDETERMINED and the missing cells are named. Cells that are not applicable to the layout are not required. Undetermined is never reported as resisted, denied, kept or suppressed.

superseded_fields: Summaries written by the runner at commit a329127 carried 'layouts_also_resisting_both_suppression_operations', computed after dropping not_run cells; it overstated resistance wherever disk-fill cells were not run. It is replaced by protection_assessment, which is three-valued.

not_run.reason: the recorder identity could not open the descriptor (O_WRONLY): PermissionError: Operation not permitted
the recorder identity could not open the descriptor (O_WRONLY|O_APPEND): PermissionError: Operation not permitted
not applicable: the transcript is already owned by the agent account, so chown would be a no-op
not applicable: this layout sets no append-only/immutable inode flag
not applicable: the recorder cannot append to an immutable transcript even on an empty filesystem, so no fill is needed to stop it

limitations: Synthetic files and explicit syscall probes; not native transcript protection and not an agent trial.
Legitimate-operation controls are synthetic proxies, not native Codex logging or resume tests.
The current wrapper runs the native recorder and agent tools under one UID; the separate-recorder layouts describe a configuration that does not exist in the wrapper yet.
In-process built-in edit tools run with the recorder's own authority and are not modelled.
Inherited-descriptor controls pass a descriptor deliberately; whether a real harness leaks one to tool processes is unknown.

Results depend on kernel, filesystem and sysctls (fs.protected_hardlinks, fs.protected_regular); a result from one environment is not a result for another, and cells not executed in an environment are undetermined there.

Disk-exhaustion suppression depends on the filesystem layout and per-filesystem quotas; the probe fills small dedicated tmpfs mounts, so its ENOSPC timing is not the production filesystem's. In docker mode the fill controls are not executed at all.
The precreate control's fallback step is refused by the file mode before fs.protected_regular is consulted, so the probe matrix does not show that sysctl's effect.
